_comment: Producer / consumer example using rt-app's suspend/resume primitives. The 'consumer' begins suspended (suspend: 'consumer' — wait on its own named event). Each iteration the 'producer' runs for 2ms, signals the consumer (resume: 'consumer'), runs another 2ms, then sleeps 5ms. The consumer wakes, runs for 1ms processing the 'work', and re-suspends. This pattern is the rt-app equivalent of a wait/signal queue and is what scxsim uses internally for crates/scx_simulator/workloads/simple_wake.json. Useful for observing wake-up paths, run-queue insertion ordering, and how a scheduler handles a producer that is the *only* source of runnable work for the consumer.
_run_units: rt-app 'run'/'sleep' are microseconds; 'suspend'/'resume' values are arbitrary event names that pair across tasks.
